Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, Richard Weitz, a senior fellow at the NATO Defence College and security analyst at Wikistrat, reflects on that day and its lasting impact. He recalls the confusion after the first plane hit, before the scale of the attacks became clear once the second plane struck and the Pentagon was hit.

Weitz says the biggest change since has been the shift in US foreign policy, from the hopeful, domestically focused 1990s to an extraordinarily interventionist era. The US invasion of Afghanistan was understandable, he says, but the subsequent war in Iraq created problems, including with Iran, that persist today. He also argues the US "dropped the ball" on China and Russia, allowing both to become potential adversaries.

US President Donald Trump is visiting Ireland on Saturday, combining diplomacy with a trip to his own golf resort. He will meet Ireland's prime minister and president at state residences in Dublin's Phoenix Park, before heading west to Doonbeg, which is hosting the Irish Open, keeping him away from planned protests in the capital.

Polls suggest most Irish people oppose the visit, but economic ties with the US run deep. 

Independent businesses have felt the fallout from Trump's tariffs, with shop owner Clare Grennan describing the scramble to keep shipping to American customers. Protesters, including lawmaker Richard Boyd Barrett, cite anger over Trump's role in the war in Gaza, strong Irish support for Palestinians, and rising energy and fuel costs.

Al Jazeera's Milena Veselinovic reports from Dublin.

description:
Russia's drone and missile campaign against Ukraine appears to be entering a new phase, with strikes over the past two days targeting fuel stations in Kyiv, another sign the air campaign against the capital is expanding.

On Thursday, an air strike hit a petrol station in Kyiv. By the time journalists arrived, the injured had already been taken to hospital and clean-up was under way. 

On Friday, Russia hit two more stations, with a double strike on one, a drone followed fifteen minutes later by another. 

All the stations hit belong to the state company Ukrnafta and are among 18 Kyiv fuel stations identified as targets in intercepted Russian communications. Motorists in the city say they now plan routes around air-raid alerts, calling it one more threat to already precarious lives.

Al Jazeera's Rory Challands reports from Kyiv.

Commemorations have taken place across the US to mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, with ceremonies held at the sites targeted that day in New York and at the Pentagon. Families of victims gathered at the 9/11 Memorial at Ground Zero, alongside Vice President JD Vance and four former US presidents.


The memorial site, once buried in rubble that took eight months to clear and years to rebuild, also marked a first this year: a moment of silence for the many more who have died since from illnesses linked to the attacks. Security was tight, with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani joining the vice president and former presidents at the ceremony.

Al Jazeera's Kristen Saloomey reports from New York.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, his first trip to India in seven years, where he is expected to hold bilateral talks with Indian leader Narendra Modi. The world's two most populous nations are working to repair a relationship that hit a low in 2020.

That year, deadly clashes between Indian and Chinese troops in the Galwan Valley, in the Himalayas, killed at least 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers, triggering a military stand-off and a deep diplomatic freeze. Trade and investment dropped, travel routes were cancelled, and political dialogue was suspended.

Ties began to thaw in 2024, when Xi and Modi met at the BRICS summit in Russia, and again in 2025 at a Shanghai Cooperation Organization meeting in China. 

For Beijing, warming ties with Delhi is part of a wider push to project China as a stable global partner, ahead of Xi's expected Washington visit for talks with Trump this month.

Al Jazeera's Katrina Yu reports from Beijing.

At least 29 students have died after a fire tore through two schools and the surrounding neighbourhood in Bukavu, in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Hundreds of homes were also destroyed, leaving thousands of families without shelter. A day later, survivors are returning to the ruins, some searching for anything they can save, others already rebuilding.

Many homes in Bukavu are built close together using timber and other flammable materials, making fires difficult to contain.

Authorities have declared three days of mourning, but survivors say they cannot wait for help and need somewhere to sleep now.

Al Jazeera's Alain Uaykani reports from Bukavu.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Across the US, memorials have been held to mark 25 years since the September 11 attacks and remember the lives lost. Al Jazeera spoke to Art Castellano, a deputy sheriff in Arlington County who was just outside the Pentagon when American Airlines Flight 77 struck the building.

Coming home afterwards brought no relief, he says, describing lasting guilt over those who did not make it out. For thousands of first responders, the toll of that day continued for years, as mental health struggles and exposure to toxic dust and chemicals took a lasting physical toll, with many not warned of the health risks until people began falling ill.

Twenty-five years on, Castellano has one message for the next generation: keep it in your heart.

Al Jazeera's Tanya Noury reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
India is hosting the BRICS summit for the fourth time, at a difficult moment both globally and within the bloc. Since Brazil, Russia, India and China formed the BRIC group in 2006, the alliance has grown to 11 members, with South Africa joining in 2010 and Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE joining in 2024 under the label BRICS+.

Together, the bloc represents nearly half the world's population, 40 percent of global GDP, 26 percent of global trade and 44 percent of global crude oil production, making it a counterweight to Western-led institutions like the G7.

But growth has brought new divisions. As host, New Delhi faces a delicate balancing act, with the bloc's 20th anniversary raising questions about whether its expanded membership can empower the Global South.

Al Jazeera's Um-e-Kulsoom Shariff reports from New Delhi.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The UN Security Council has voted 15-0 to extend its arms embargo on Sudan's Darfur region, but only for another four weeks. The resolution is a holding pattern rather than a decision, after the United States failed to win support for expanding the ban across all of Sudan.

Washington's deputy ambassador Jeffrey Bartos pointed to an airstrike on a World Food Programme convoy in South Kordofan, outside the embargo's current reach, arguing inaction meant more suffering. Russia and China objected, saying Sudan's army needs weapons to hold its advantage against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

Sudan's government also opposed a countrywide embargo, arguing it would wrongly equate its national army with militias and foreign fighters. The embargo dates back to 2004, before the RSF existed under that name, and UN experts say weapons are reaching both sides of the war.
